exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Password Guessing
exploitedBy.relevance: Default or weak credentials are directly exploitable via password guessing attacks against database authentication.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Password Cracking
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak database credentials are susceptible to offline password cracking techniques.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credential Stuffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Default credentials are commonly included in credential stuffing lists used to gain unauthorized database access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Sniffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted database connections can be intercepted via network sniffing, exposing credentials and sensitive data in transit.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Databases
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted data at rest in databases can be directly accessed and exfiltrated if storage is compromised.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Stored Data Manipulation
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted stored data is vulnerable to manipulation by adversaries who gain access to storage.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Service Discovery
exploitedBy.relevance: Publicly exposed database ports can be discovered by adversaries performing network service scanning.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Search Open Technical Databases
exploitedBy.relevance: Exposed database ports may be indexed by internet scanning services, enabling adversaries to discover them passively.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Valid Accounts
exploitedBy.relevance: Overprivileged database accounts, once compromised, allow adversaries to abuse valid credentials with excessive permissions.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Account Manipulation
exploitedBy.relevance: Adversaries may manipulate overprivileged database accounts to maintain persistence or escalate privileges.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Disable or Modify Cloud Logs
exploitedBy.relevance: Disabling or failing to configure audit logging mirrors this technique of suppressing log collection to avoid detection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Disable or Modify Linux Audit System
exploitedBy.relevance: Incomplete or disabled database audit logging is analogous to disabling the Linux audit system, hindering forensic investigation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Disable Windows Event Logging
exploitedBy.relevance: Disabled database audit logging reduces visibility into malicious activity, similar to disabling event logging.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
exploitedBy.relevance: Unpatched database engines are vulnerable to known exploits targeting public-facing database services.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Known vulnerabilities in unpatched database engines can be exploited remotely to gain unauthorized access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
exploitedBy.relevance: Unpatched database engine vulnerabilities may be leveraged for privilege escalation on the host system.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data from Information Repositories
exploitedBy.relevance: Unauthenticated access enables adversaries to collect data from information repositories without needing credentials.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data from Cloud Storage
exploitedBy.relevance: Backup files without access controls in cloud storage can be accessed by adversaries to exfiltrate sensitive data.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials In Files
exploitedBy.relevance: Database backup files may contain credentials that adversaries can harvest if stored without proper access controls.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Unsecured Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Storing secrets in plaintext configuration files represents unsecured credentials that adversaries can easily discover and abuse.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Private Keys
exploitedBy.relevance: Configuration files may contain private keys or tokens stored in plaintext, exposing cryptographic material to adversaries.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Service Exhaustion Flood
exploitedBy.relevance: Without connection rate limiting, databases are vulnerable to service exhaustion floods that can cause denial of service.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Application Exhaustion Flood
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of max connection enforcement enables application-layer exhaustion attacks against the database service.
